chief_complaint: progressive ptosis, double vision, and fatigue worse at night
hpi_details: A 50-year-old female presents to the clinic with progressive ptosis, double vision, and fatigue worse at night. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks her droopy eyelids and double vision are just severe eye strain and fatigue from staring at computer screens all day.
concerns: She is worried that she might have a car accident on her evening commute because of the double vision.
expectations: She hopes to get a referral to a specialist eye clinic and a prescription for eye drops to prop her eyelids open.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Myasthenia Gravis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Myasthenia Gravis: Pyridostigmine, Prednisone, check thymoma, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Key HPI features: A 50-year-old female presents to the clinic with progressive ptosis, double vision, and fatigue worse at night. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Myasthenia Gravis.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Myasthenia Gravis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Lambert-Eaton syndrome without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Breathing difficulty.
management_principles: Plan for Myasthenia Gravis: Pyridostigmine, Prednisone, check thymoma
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of progressive ptosis, double vision, and fatigue worse at night. HPI: autoantibodies against ACh receptors.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Myasthenia Gravis.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Myasthenia Gravis.
reference_soap.plan: Arrange prompt neurology evaluation to confirm myasthenia gravis and assess for thymoma; treatment may include pyridostigmine and immunotherapy under specialist guidance. Send the patient for emergency assessment for breathing, swallowing, or rapidly worsening weakness.

teaching.one_liner: Autoantibodies against acetylcholine receptors causing progressive ptosis, double vision, and fatigue worse at night.

must_ask.say: Do symptoms worsen as the day goes on?
Any drooping eyelids or double vision?
How many months has this been going on?

history.answer: My eyelids have been drooping and I've been seeing double lately, especially towards the end of the day.
It started gradually about three weeks ago and has been slowly getting worse.
Both of my eyelids droop, but my left side is noticeably more droopy than my right.
My vision does not black out completely, but the double vision comes and goes depending on how tired I am.
The objects themselves look clear, but they split into two separate images side by side rather than being blurry or distorted in the center.
I notice the double vision both up close and far away, and I have not had any changes in my eyeglasses prescription.
I do not have glare or halos around headlights, though driving at night is tough because of the double vision.
No, I have not seen any floating spots, flashes of light, or any dark shadow like a curtain falling over my eyes.
Yes, I see two distinct images, and the second image disappears completely whenever I cover or close either eye.
My eyelids droop much lower by evening, but when I wake up in the morning after a good sleep, they are almost normal.
Yes, taking a short nap or resting with my eyes closed for twenty minutes helps my vision and eyelids improve temporarily.
My jaw muscles feel tired and weak when I chew tough foods like steak, but I have not had trouble swallowing liquids or pills.
No, my breathing has been completely normal without any shortness of breath.
No, I have no pain in or behind my eyes, no pain when moving them, and no redness.
No, I have not had any new headaches, no tenderness over my temples when brushing my hair, and no shoulder aching.
My arms feel tired and heavy when I blow-dry my hair, but I have no numbness, tingling, slurred speech, or dizziness.
No, I have never had any injury to my head, face, or eyes.
No, I do not have diabetes or high blood pressure, and my last routine checkup with the eye doctor was completely normal.
No, I have never been diagnosed with heart rhythm problems like atrial fibrillation or any blocked blood vessels in my neck.
No, I do not have high myopia, glaucoma, or cataracts, and I have never had surgery on my eyes.
I do not take steroids, hydroxychloroquine, tuberculosis medications, or any regular prescription eye drops.
It makes reading and driving in the evening very hard, so I have had to stop driving at night, though I have not fallen.
I assumed my eyes are just exhausted from staring at computer screens all day at work and that I need stronger bifocals.
I'm really terrified I'm going to crash my car driving home from work in the dark because my eyes keep crossing.
I was hoping to get a referral to an ophthalmologist and maybe some eye drops or a patch to help me see straight.
I have generally been very healthy and have no history of chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgical operations or hospital admissions in the past.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I only drink a glass of wine socially once or twice a month, and nothing more.
I work as an office accountant and live at home with my husband and teenage daughter.
No one in my family has autoimmune disorders, muscle diseases, glaucoma, or blindness.
My menstrual cycles have become irregular over the past year as I enter menopause, with my last period two months ago, and there is no chance of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.6 C, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
Alert and oriented in no acute distress, with visible bilateral eyelid drooping that is slightly more prominent on the left.
Bilateral temporal arteries are soft, nontender, and normally pulsating.

Corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, pupils are equal, round, and briskly reactive to light with no afferent defect, visual fields are full to confrontation, and funduscopic exam shows sharp disc margins and healthy retinas.

Bilateral ptosis worsens noticeably after forty-five seconds of sustained upgaze, with disconjugated extraocular movements producing binocular diplopia, while pupillary reflexes, facial sensation, and palate elevation remain intact.
Normal muscle bulk and tone, with mild fatigable weakness in bilateral deltoids after repetitive testing (4/5), while distal upper extremity and lower extremity strength remain 5/5.
Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric throughout without post-exercise potentiation, and plantar responses are flexor bilaterally.
Light touch, pinprick, vibration, and joint position senses are fully intact in all four extremities.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with unlabored breathing and normal respiratory excursion.
